segments.text:
Verſ. 5.
And the ſtrangers ſhall ſtand and feede your ſheep: and the ſonnes of the ſtrangers ſhall be your plowmen, and dreſſers of your vines.

HIs meaning is, that the ſtrangers ſhall bee readie to obey them. For in reſpect they were at that time diuided from other nations, no man would lend them their hand. And therefore hee ſaith, that the ſtrangers doe ſtand: that is to ſay, are readie preſt to meete and to ſuccour them.

Where he addes, that they ſhall feede their ſheepe and ſhall be the plowmen and vinedreſſers, theſe are borowed kinds of ſpeeches. For the Prophet ſpeakes of Chriſts kingdome, which is ſpirituall; and ſets foorth the perfect felicitie thereof, vnder theſe figures; that we might the better conceiue of thoſe things which are here propoſed vnto vs by examples. Let vs know therefore that wee ſhall bee truely happie, when Chriſt ſhall reigne ouer vs: for by meanes thereof many commodities whereof the poſteritie of Adam is worthily depriued, ſhall be reſtored vnto vs vnawares.
